# CHAIN

## Syntax

```synesis
FIELD <name> TYPE CHAIN
    SCOPE <scope>
    ARITY <operator> <n>
    [RELATIONS ... END RELATIONS]
    [DESCRIPTION <text>]
    [GUIDELINES ... END GUIDELINES]
    [CONTEXT FROM DATASET <section>]
END FIELD
```

`[ ]` optional · `<>` value to replace

## Example

```synesis
FIELD example_chain TYPE CHAIN
    SCOPE ITEM
    ARITY >= 2
END FIELD
```

## Value in the annotation

A qualified chain alternates concepts and relations; a simple chain has only concepts:

```synesis
chain: phishing -> EXPLOITS -> trust
```

Each relation must be declared in the field `RELATIONS` (`SYNESIS_E010`). Several `chain:` lines in one ITEM are several chains, and each pairs with its own BUNDLE partners by position.

## Properties

| Property | Status | Error if violated |
|---|---|---|
| `CONTEXT FROM DATASET` | Allowed | - |
| `DESCRIPTION` | Allowed | - |
| `GUIDELINES` | Allowed | - |
| `RELATIONS` | Allowed | - |
| `FORMAT` | Forbidden | SYNESIS_E054 |
| `VALUES` | Forbidden | SYNESIS_E086 |
| `ARITY` | Required | SYNESIS_E047 |

## Rules

- **`ARITY` is required.** The field 'field_name' is of type CHAIN, but does not declare `ARITY`.
